newsitem.title: FINLAND: KCI SAYS 97 SALES MAY EXCEED FIM 3 BLN. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: KCI SAYS 97 SALES MAY EXCEED FIM 3 BLN. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]

text.p: Finnish cranemaker KCI Konecranes International (KCI) CEO Stig Gustavsson said on Thursday full-year net sales may exceed three billion markka this year.

"Analysts' forecasts are around three billion, some over; and I have no objections to that based on the current orders," Gustavsson told analysts and journalists in a briefing after the company announced in-line January-April earnings.
"The orderstock points to 20 percent volume growth, and that is a good thing," he said adding that this year would be marked by strong growth overall.
KCI's 1996 net sales were 2.45 billion markka.
KCI said earlier that group earnings for the full-year were expected to be in line with the group's long-term targets.

Gustavsson showed a table of KCI's five-year targets which put the operating margin at 10 percent, average return on equity at above 25 percent, EPS growth at 15 percent or more, and gearing at 35 percent or less.
A 15 percent increase in EPS over last year's 9.26 markka earnings per share would put it at 10.7 markka. First tertial EPS was 1.67 markka, down from 1.69 in the year-ago period.
Gustavsson said the first tertial profit -- up just 2.5 percent at 37.1 million markka -- was not indicative for the full year for two reasons:
- Licencing royalties in the first tertial fell to 0.5 million markka from 8 million, but this was a fluctuation and the market was still steady and royalties were seen picking up.
- Operating profit excluding royalties rose 30 percent (corrects from 38 percent), but this was "also not indicative, the full year figure will level out", Konecranes said.
Konecranes said last week it agreed with the median of analysts' full-year forecasts in a Reuters poll -- 250 million markka after financial items versus 208.2 million in 1996.
